task_payload.focus: Audit Click's public export layer, decorators, command core, parser, and testing harness.

tests_or_commands_run: probe_m1nd tools + trust/selftest on the repo-local runtime
probe_m1nd ingest + audit + seek/search/recovery_playbook on the click lane fixture
rg/sed/nl on src/click/{__init__,decorators,core,parser,types,testing}.py
task_results.notes: Proven structure: `__init__.py` is the public export layer; `decorators.py` turns callbacks plus memoized params into `Command`/`Group` objects; `core.py` owns context creation, parameter parsing, and subcommand dispatch; `parser.py` is the low-level argv tokenizer; `types.py` owns custom type adaptation; and `testing.py` is the IO-isolating harness. Proven risk concentration: `core.py` and `testing.py` are the highest-blast-radius files. Hypothesis only: shell-completion and platform-specific termui branches deserve separate runtime smokes.
evidence: Public API re-exports are centralized in src/click/__init__.py:10-74, which forwards core classes, decorators, exceptions, termui helpers, and common types.

Decorator-to-command conversion happens in src/click/decorators.py:221-249, where memoized params are recovered from `__click_params__`, a name is derived, and `cls(...)` instantiates the command object.
Command invocation enters through src/click/core.py:1210-1281 (`make_context` + `parse_args`) and then flows through src/click/core.py:1867-1901 for group dispatch and subcommand invocation.
Low-level argv parsing lives in src/click/parser.py:265-314, where `_OptionParser` collects option definitions and returns `(values, args, order)` to `Command.parse_args`.

Parameter/type conversion crosses src/click/core.py:2179-2182 and src/click/types.py:1218-1259, where `Option.__init__` calls `convert_type(...)` and custom callables become `FuncParamType` instances.

Test runner IO isolation is implemented in src/click/testing.py:312-401 and 582-625, where `CliRunner.isolation` swaps `sys.stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr` and `CliRunner.invoke` executes `cli.main(...)` inside that redirected environment.

task_payload.flow: Explain what happens when setup_panic!() is installed and a release-mode panic occurs.

tests_or_commands_run: probe_m1nd ingest + search setup_panic!/Metadata/homepage on the human-panic lane fixture
sed/nl on src/lib.rs, src/panic.rs, src/report.rs, and tests/single-panic/tests/integration.rs
task_results.notes: Release-mode here means `PanicStyle::Human`: a panic hook is installed, a `Report` is built from `PanicHookInfo`, the report is persisted unless `CI` is set, and then the friendly crash message is printed to stderr. Debug builds or `RUST_BACKTRACE` skip that human hook path.
evidence: The public entrypoint is the `setup_panic!` macro in src/lib.rs:98-106, which expands to `$crate::setup_panic(|| $meta)` and defaults to `metadata!()` when no explicit metadata is passed.
Default metadata comes from src/lib.rs:65-70, where `metadata!()` seeds the crate name/version plus authors/homepage/repository from Cargo env vars.
Release-mode selection happens in src/panic.rs:15-18 and 58-67: `PanicStyle::default()` returns `Human` outside debug builds when `RUST_BACKTRACE` is not set.

The panic hook body is in src/panic.rs:20-37, where `Report::with_panic(&meta, info)` is built, `report.persist().ok()` writes a file unless `CI` is set, and `print_msg(file_path.as_deref(), &meta)` emits the user-facing stderr text.
Report creation and persistence are in src/report.rs:67-110, where `with_panic(...)` derives explanation/cause fields and `persist()` writes `report-<uuid>.toml` into `env::temp_dir()`.

Observable output is proven in tests/single-panic/tests/integration.rs:12-28 and 123-147: release mode prints the human message plus report path, while `CI=1` prints serialized report data to stderr and skips writing a file.

task_payload.symptom: A callable instance used as a custom Click option type crashes during command construction with AttributeError because the object has no __name__ attribute.
must_answer: why it is not a parser/runtime invocation issue

tests_or_commands_run: probe_m1nd search on the click type-conversion path and shell reads on core/types
uv run --locked --no-default-groups --group tests pytest tests/test_m1nd_seeded_callable_type.py
task_results.notes: Most likely fault boundary is `FuncParamType.__init__` in `src/click/types.py`, reached from `Option.__init__` via `types.convert_type(...)` while the decorator stack is still constructing the command object. This is not a parser/runtime invocation issue because `Command.make_context` and `Command.parse_args` only run after the command already exists. Alternative theory rejected: callback name normalization in `decorators.command` touches the CLI function, not the custom `type=` instance.
evidence: Command construction crosses src/click/core.py:2179-2182, where `Option.__init__` eagerly calls `types.convert_type(type, default)`.
Custom callable adaptation ends in src/click/types.py:1218-1259, where non-`ParamType` callables are wrapped as `FuncParamType(guessed)`.
The failing boundary is src/click/types.py:185-188, where `FuncParamType.__init__` reads `func.__name__`; callable instances like `UpperCase()` do not define that attribute.
The focused regression test is tests/test_m1nd_seeded_callable_type.py:10-19, which constructs a command with `type=UpperCase()` and verifies the command both builds and runs.

task_payload.claim: README/docs say Click supports lazy loading of subcommands at runtime.

tests_or_commands_run: probe_m1nd search "lazy loading" plus recovery_playbook on the click lane fixture
sed/nl on README.md, docs/index.rst, docs/complex.md, and src/click/core.py
task_results.notes: Conclusion: partial docs drift. The top-level README/index bullets are directionally true at the API level, but they over-read as a built-in feature. The deeper `docs/complex.md` explanation matches the code: lazy loading is implemented by a custom `Group` subclass that overrides `list_commands` and `get_command`, while the base `Group` remains dict-backed.
evidence: The public claim appears in README.md:16-18 and docs/index.rst:21-23, both of which say Click “supports lazy loading of subcommands at runtime.”
The detailed pattern in docs/complex.md:224-228 and 261-269 is narrower: a custom `Group` subclass stores extra metadata, extends `list_commands`, and makes `get_command` perform the import.
Actual base behavior is simpler in src/click/core.py:1806-1814, where `Group.get_command` just does `self.commands.get(cmd_name)` and `list_commands` just sorts `self.commands`.

The support hook is still real: src/click/core.py:1636-1638, 1830-1831, and 1940-1947 show that help rendering and command resolution repeatedly call `get_command`/`list_commands`, which is why the custom lazy-group pattern works.
